subject: Is selecting columns range with facets possible ?

messages.author: 62b227645680b44d
messages.subject: Is selecting columns range with facets possible ?
parts:
Hi,

Assuming I have data.frame with columns Treatment Subject and each row has label for levels, those are factors. I know I can use them in facets, but in a multivariate data I also have columns with different names for instance measured variables VAR1...VAR10. I would like to display plot for each variable. Now they only way I know is by specifying manually every time which variable I want on Y axis, is it possible to make this more automatic possibly by facets ? I would like for example to say make all possible plots for 4:10 variables with xaxis as showing as treatment and yaxis corresponding value for that variable.

Simple example

Treatment Subject Var1 Var2 Var3 ... Var10
A              1           1      4        7        5
B              1           2      5        8        6
C              1           3      6        9        7

I would like to have plots Treatment vs Var4, Treatment vs Var5, Treatment vs Var6 .... and so on.

Can I use facets for that ?

Thanks,

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: Is selecting columns range with facets possible ?
parts:
It can be done, but it requires that melt the data so it's in long format.

require(reshape)
molten_data <- melt(data, id.vars = c("Treatment", "Subject"))

qplot(Treatment, value, data = molten_data) + 
     facet_wrap(~ variable)

HTH
Luciano
